examples.ko: 우리 집은 현관 옆 구석방을 창고로 써요.
examples.en: At our house, we use the corner room next to the entrance as storage.

examples.ko: 그 방은 구석방이라서 낮에도 좀 어두워요.
examples.en: That room is in a corner, so it's a bit dark even in the daytime.

examples.ko: 대학 때 복도 끝 구석방에서 살았어요.
examples.en: In college I lived in the room at the far corner of the hallway.
I shut myself in the back room alone and just played games.
The sunlight coming through the back room's window is warm.
The back room is quiet, so it's good for studying.

explain: 집이나 건물의 한쪽 구석에 있는 방을 말해요. 크기가 작고 외진 방은 '골방'이라고도 해요. 거실이나 안방처럼 중심이 되는 방과 대비해서 써요.
explain_en: It refers to a room tucked into a corner of a house or building. A small, remote room can also be called a '골방'. It is used in contrast with central rooms such as the living room or main bedroom.

en: last farm products of the season; last sea products of the season

examples.ko: 딸기가 이제 끝물이라서 값이 많이 싸졌어요.
examples.en: Strawberries are at the end of their season now, so the price has dropped a lot.

examples.ko: 이 복숭아는 끝물이라 맛이 조금 덜해요.
examples.en: These peaches are at the end of the season, so they taste a little less good.

examples.ko: 여름 과일은 끝물에 사면 더 싸게 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can buy summer fruit cheaper at the end of its season.

examples.ko: 벌써 오징어도 끝물이라고 시장 아저씨가 말했어요.
examples.en: The man at the market said squid is already at the end of its season too.
Even though it is the end of the season, these grapes are very sweet.

examples.ko: 제철 과일은 끝물이 되기 전에 먹어 두세요.
examples.en: Eat seasonal fruit before it reaches the end of its season.

explain: '제철'은 한창 맛있을 때이고, '끝물'은 그 철이 거의 끝나 가는 때예요. 시장에서 "끝물이라 싸요"처럼 자주 들려요. 반대로 그해에 처음 나온 것에는 '햇감자', '햇과일'처럼 '햇-'을 붙여요.
explain_en: '제철' is the peak of the season, while '끝물' is when the season is nearly over. You often hear it at markets, as in '끝물이라 싸요' (it's cheap because the season is ending). For the first produce of the year, people attach '햇-', as in '햇감자' (new potatoes) and '햇과일' (new-season fruit).

examples.en: The negotiations are running into difficulty.
The construction ran into trouble because of the rain.
The meeting is stuck, so it didn't end today either.

examples.ko: 두 회사의 합병 논의는 난항을 거듭하고 있어요.
examples.en: The merger talks between the two companies keep hitting snags.
The work was finally wrapped up after a rough time.

examples.ko: 난항이 예상되지만 포기하지 말고 해 봐요.
examples.en: We expect a tough time, but let's try without giving up.

explain: 원래는 험한 항해나 비행을 뜻하지만, 지금은 일이나 협상이 잘 풀리지 않을 때 더 많이 써요. '난항을 겪다', '난항에 부딪히다', '난항을 거듭하다'로 자주 말하고 뉴스에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It originally means a rough voyage or flight, but today it is used more for work or negotiations that are not going smoothly. Typical forms are '난항을 겪다', '난항에 부딪히다' and '난항을 거듭하다', and it is common in the news.

en: to be paying no heed; to have no concern with

examples.ko: 그는 남들 시선에 아랑곳없이 큰 소리로 노래했어요.
examples.en: He sang loudly, paying no mind to others' stares.

examples.ko: 비가 오는 것에 아랑곳없이 아이들이 뛰어놀아요.
examples.en: The kids run around playing, unbothered by the rain.

examples.ko: 주변 사람이 뭐라고 하든 저는 아랑곳없어요.
examples.en: I don't care what the people around me say.
I envy his attitude of not caring what others say.

examples.ko: 추위에 아랑곳없이 사람들이 줄을 서 있었어요.
examples.en: People stood in line, regardless of the cold.
No matter how much we tried to stop him, he paid no heed.

explain: 대부분 '~에 아랑곳없이'처럼 쓰고, '~에 아랑곳하지 않고'라고도 해요. 주변 시선이나 날씨, 충고를 신경 쓰지 않고 자기 할 일을 계속하는 모습에 어울려요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '~에 아랑곳없이', and you can also say '~에 아랑곳하지 않고'. It fits someone who keeps doing their own thing without minding stares, weather or advice.

en: cold spell of winter; frigid winter

examples.ko: 엄동설한에 길에서 떨고 있는 사람들을 도왔어요.
examples.en: We helped the people shivering on the street in the bitter winter cold.
It's the dead of winter, so the water pipes froze and burst.
Where are you going in this freezing winter weather?
Even in the harshest winter, the market is crowded with people.
The boiler broke in the dead of winter, and we had a hard time.

examples.ko: 엄동설한의 추위를 견디며 먹을 것을 구했대요.
examples.en: They say they endured the bitter winter cold while searching for food.

explain: 눈이 오고 몹시 추운 한겨울을 가리키는 말이에요. '한겨울'보다 매섭고 힘든 느낌이 있고, 말투가 약간 무겁고 예스러워서 이야기나 글에서 자주 나와요. 보통 '엄동설한에'처럼 때를 나타내는 말로 써요.
explain_en: It points to the deep winter when it is snowy and very cold. It feels harsher and more hardship-filled than '한겨울', and the tone is a bit heavy and old-fashioned, so it appears often in stories and writing. It is usually used as a time expression like '엄동설한에'.

examples.ko: 어제 커피를 연거푸 세 잔이나 마셨어요.
examples.en: Yesterday I drank three cups of coffee in a row.
That player won the championship repeatedly in a row.
I made mistakes one after another and felt so embarrassed.
Maybe because I breathed in smoke, I coughed again and again.

examples.ko: 시험에서 연거푸 떨어져도 포기하지 않을 거예요.
examples.en: Even if I fail the exam repeatedly, I won't give up.

examples.ko: 연거푸 비가 와서 빨래를 못 말렸어요.
examples.en: It rained day after day, so I couldn't dry my laundry.

explain: '계속'은 오래 이어지는 느낌이고, '연거푸'는 같은 일이 짧은 간격으로 잇달아 여러 번 일어날 때 써요. 잔, 번, 실수처럼 셀 수 있는 일과 잘 어울리고, '연달아', '잇따라'와 비슷해요.
explain_en: '계속' (continuously) suggests something going on for a long time, while '연거푸' means the same thing happens several times in quick succession. It pairs well with countable things like cups, times and mistakes, and is close to '연달아' and '잇따라'.

examples.en: Tomorrow is the first day of autumn, but it's still so hot.
Once ipchu passes, the breeze changes in the mornings and evenings.
According to the calendar, this year's ipchu is August 7.
Just because it's ipchu doesn't mean it suddenly gets cool.

examples.ko: 입추를 하루 앞두고 날씨가 푹푹 쪄요.
examples.en: The day before ipchu, the weather is sweltering.

examples.ko: 어제가 입추였는데 전혀 가을 같지 않았어요.
examples.en: Yesterday was ipchu, but it didn't feel like autumn at all.

explain: 달력으로는 가을이 시작되는 날이지만, 우리나라에서는 보통 아직 한창 더울 때예요. 다른 계절의 시작을 나타내는 '입춘', '입하', '입동'과 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: By the calendar it is the first day of autumn, but in Korea it is usually still the hottest part of summer. It helps to learn it together with 입춘, 입하 and 입동, which mark the start of the other seasons.

examples.en: There are many skyscrapers in Seoul.
From a high-rise apartment, you can see the whole city at a glance.
The wind blows hard around skyscrapers.

examples.ko: 새로 지은 초고층 호텔에서 하룻밤 잤어요.
examples.en: I stayed one night at a newly built high-rise hotel.
Riding a skyscraper elevator makes my ears feel blocked.

examples.ko: 초고층에 사는 친구가 있어서 가끔 놀러 가요.
examples.en: I have a friend who lives high up, so I visit sometimes.

explain: '초고층 아파트', '초고층 빌딩'처럼 건물 앞에 붙여서 써요. '고층'은 높은 층이고 '초고층'은 그보다 훨씬 높은 건물이에요. 뉴스나 부동산 이야기에서 많이 나오고, 같은 뜻의 '마천루'는 글에서 가끔 써요.
explain_en: It goes before building words: '초고층 아파트', '초고층 빌딩'. '고층' means high floors, while '초고층' is far taller. It is common in news and real estate talk; the synonym '마천루' appears occasionally in writing.

en: lean year; year of poor harvest

examples.en: There was a poor harvest, so the price of rice rose a lot.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 흉년이 들면 굶는 사람이 많았어요.
examples.en: In the old days, when the harvest failed, many people went hungry.

examples.ko: 올해는 비가 너무 많이 와서 흉년이에요.
examples.en: This year it rained too much, so it's a lean harvest year.
That year the apple harvest was very poor.
I heard neighbors shared with one another even in lean years.

examples.ko: 풍년과 흉년이 번갈아 온다고 할머니가 말씀하셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother said good harvests and bad harvests come by turns.

explain: 농사가 잘 안 된 해를 말하고, 반대말은 '풍년'이에요. 보통 '흉년이 들다'로 말하는데, 뉴스나 요즘 대화에서는 같은 뜻으로 '흉작'도 많이 써요. 옛날이야기나 역사 수업에서도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means a year when the harvest went badly, and its opposite is '풍년'. It is usually said as '흉년이 들다', and '흉작' is a related word often used in news and modern talk. It also comes up often in old stories and history lessons.
